---
title: "The decision for an isolated pair"
subtitle: "2.1 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 10, and Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), slides 18–20"
description: "Posterior expected loss of the two strict directions and withholding for a single pair."
---

When exact equality has zero posterior probability, the two directions cost $1-\pi_{AB}$ and $\pi_{AB}$, where $\pi_{AB}=\Pr(\theta_A>\theta_B\mid Y)$. Withholding costs $\tau$. The lowest line gives the best action.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **π .85, τ .10.** Error $e_{AB}$ = .15 exceeds τ = .10, so the lowest-cost action is to withhold.
- **π .85, τ .20.** Raising τ to .20 lifts only the horizontal line; $e_{AB}$ stays .15, selecting “state A above B”.
- **π .80, τ .20.** At $e_{AB}$ = .20 = τ, stating A above B and withholding are “equally good” at the open-circle crossing.
- **π .50, τ .50.** All three costs equal .50, so “all three actions are equally good”.

```{=html}
<details>
<summary>Isolated-pair rule and multi-pair reports</summary>
<p>With zero posterior probability of equal true values, an isolated pair discloses a direction only when its posterior probability exceeds 1 &minus; &tau; (tying with withholding at equality). A shared grade withholds a direction rather than asserting equal true values; combining many pair decisions into one coherent report adds a global transitivity constraint beyond this isolated-pair rule.</p>
</details>
```
